To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the forecast skill of the ice extent for the Arctic Ocean is 0.75 relative to the climatological mean for 11 months of lead time.
the ice extent in the pan-arctic ocean is predictable with a skill of about 0.8 for lead periods of 6 months and 0.7 for lead periods of one year.

(1) the empirical model is able to predict the pan-arctic sea-ice extent for the following year with skill relative to climatology that exceeds 75% for six months lead, (2) the ocean temperature at 200–270 m depth is the best single predictor of ice extent for lead times of six months and longer, and (3) the forecast skill is reduced when detrended data are used, suggesting that the model is capturing the trend in ice extent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of the extent of sea ice in the Arctic Ocean for lead times up to one year.
the predictability of the ice extent of the Arctic Ocean and the factors that contribute to the predictability.
the development of a statistical model for predicting the pan-Arctic ice extent and regional ice extents.
